docs.title: PlexusHive
docs.text:
Formats and tools for coordinating long-lived coding agents: the work identity each agent works under, the decisions that bind them, the status reports they file, and the envelope they put on messages to each other.

When a dozen agent sessions each work for days across hundreds of repositories, the human operator ends up as the only router and the only memory. PlexusHive writes down what each agent is for, where it works, who settles conflicts in a repository, and why things were decided, in plain JSON files that every agent can read and tests can validate.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Work identities, not sessions. A work identity is durable. A session working under it declares it with HIVE_IDENTITY or plexushive start, so renaming or restarting a session changes nothing in the records.
  • Stewards, not owners. Several work identities may work in a repository; at most one stewards it and settles conflicts.
  • An append-only decision log. Decisions are superseded, never rewritten.
  • Go types are the source of truth. JSON Schemas are generated from them, and loading is strict, so a typo fails instead of being dropped.
  • Your records stay yours. This module holds the formats and code; the records live in a hive directory of your own, usually a private repository.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
my-hive/
├── identities/<name>.json  one file per work identity
├── decisions/<id>.json     the append-only decision log
└── open-items.json         questions waiting on the operator, until closed

plexushive -C my-hive validate                        # check every work identity and decision
plexushive -C my-hive identities github.com/example/web  # who works there, steward first
plexushive -C my-hive brief                           # your actions, decisions, blockers, work in progress
plexushive -C my-hive start billing                   # bind a work identity to this tmux session

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: PlexusHive needs Go 1.26 or later.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
go install github.com/plexusone/plexushive/cmd/plexushive@latest
plexushive --help

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
go get github.com/plexusone/plexushive

import "github.com/plexusone/plexushive/hive"

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Create a hive with one work identity and one decision, then validate it.

mkdir -p my-hive/work identities my-hive/decisions

my-hive/identities/billing.json:

{
  "name": "billing",
  "status": "draft",
  "mission": "Own the billing service and its payment integrations.",
  "autonomy": "prepare",
  "repositories": [
    {"pattern": "github.com/example/billing", "affinity": "steward"}
  ]
}

my-hive/decisions/one-billing-service.json:

{
  "id": "one-billing-service",
  "title": "One service owns billing",
  "status": "accepted",
  "decision": "All charges go through the billing service.",
  "reasons": ["One place to audit every charge."],
  "identities": ["billing"]
}

Validate it and ask who works in the billing repository:

$ plexushive -C my-hive validate
1 work identity and 1 decision are valid

$ plexushive -C my-hive identities github.com/example/billing
steward      billing              repository

Start the agent's session with its work identity:

HIVE_IDENTITY=billing claude --resume <session>

The User Guide covers each step in depth.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: PlexusHive keeps a written record of what each long-lived coding agent is for, where it works, and why things were decided, so the agents can coordinate without the operator relaying every message. This guide sets up a hive directory, writes work identities and decisions, and wires validation into tests and agent sessions.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Work identity What one agent is for: its mission, autonomy, the repositories it works in and its peers. Durable; outlives any session. Session The running agent (for example a terminal session) that works under a work identity. Renamed and restarted freely; no record names it. Steward The one work identity that settles conflicting and breaking changes in a repository. Others may still work there. Decision One entry in the append-only log: what was decided, why, and what was rejected. Report One work identity's current status: done, blocked, next, and decisions it needs. Kept on the machine, not in git. Envelope The first line of a message between agents: [hive] type=… from=… ref=….

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI
docs.text: go install github.com/plexusone/plexushive/cmd/plexushive@latest

docs.title: 2. Create a hive directory
docs.text:
Keep the records in a repository of your own. If they name private products or repositories, make it a private one.

my-hive/
├── identities/
│   ├── billing.json
│   └── website.json
└── decisions/
    └── stewards-not-owners.json

Each file holds one record and is named after it: identities/billing.json holds the work identity named billing. One record per file means agents writing at the same time never edit the same file.

docs.title: 3. Write a work identity
docs.text:
{
  "name": "billing",
  "status": "draft",
  "mission": "Own the billing service and its payment integrations.",
  "autonomy": "prepare",
  "repositories": [
    {"pattern": "github.com/example/billing", "affinity": "steward"},
    {"pattern": "github.com/example/web", "affinity": "collaborator"}
  ],
  "peers": ["website"]
}
  • Start a work identity as draft; set it to active once you confirm it.
  • Choose the lowest autonomy that lets the agent do its job:
  • observe reads, analyzes and reports, and changes nothing.
  • prepare also makes local changes for you to publish: branches, commits, release notes. It never pushes, tags, merges, deploys or sends.
  • execute also makes bounded, low-risk changes itself.
  • A pattern is one repository, github.com/<org>/<repo>, or a whole organization, github.com/<org>/*. At most one active work identity stewards a pattern, and an exact repository outranks an organization pattern.
  • A repository no work identity lists is common ground.

See which work identities work in a repository:

$ plexushive -C my-hive identities github.com/example/web
steward      website              repository
collaborator billing              repository

docs.title: 4. Bind a session to its work identity
docs.text:
A session declares its work identity with the HIVE_IDENTITY environment variable. Keep the binding out of the records, because sessions change:

HIVE_IDENTITY=billing claude --resume <session>

In tmux, bind it to the session once, from inside it:

plexushive -C my-hive start billing

start checks the work identity, sets HIVE_IDENTITY in the tmux session's environment and prints the work identity's context: mission, repositories, peers and how to reach them, the decisions that bind it, and how to report. Every plexushive command run in that session then finds the work identity, even in an agent that was already running, because it reads the binding back from tmux. plexushive whoami shows the work identity and where it was found.

A hook that runs when a session starts, or after its context is compacted, can run plexushive -C my-hive context to give the agent the same context again.

docs.title: 5. Record a decision
docs.text:
Write a decision when a choice will constrain later work, especially another agent's.

{
  "id": "stewards-not-owners",
  "title": "Repositories have stewards, not owners",
  "status": "accepted",
  "decision": "Several work identities may change a repository; at most one stewards it.",
  "reasons": ["Work crosses repositories, and one work identity per repository does not scale."],
  "alternatives": [
    {"option": "One owning work identity per repository", "rejected": "Forces every cross-repository change through a message."}
  ],
  "repositories": ["github.com/example/web"]
}

Decisions are append-only. To change one, write a new decision that lists the old ID in supersedes, then set the old one's status to superseded and its supersededBy to the new ID. Validation fails unless both sides agree. Leave dates out; git history records when a decision was made.

docs.title: 6. Validate
docs.text:
From the CLI:

$ plexushive -C my-hive validate
2 work identities and 1 decision are valid

Or in the hive repository's own tests, so every change is checked:

package myhive

import (
    "testing"

    "github.com/plexusone/plexushive/hive"
)

func TestRecords(t *testing.T) {
    h, err := hive.Load(".")
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := h.Validate(); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
}

Loading is strict: an unknown field, trailing data, or a file named differently from its record is an error, so a typo fails instead of being silently dropped. Validation then checks each record and the set as a whole: unique names, peers that exist, one steward per pattern, decisions that name existing work identities, and supersede links that agree.

Tools that cannot import Go can validate against the JSON Schemas:

plexushive schema identity > identity.schema.json
plexushive schema decision > decision.schema.json

docs.title: 7. Message other agents
docs.text:
Put the envelope on the first line of a message to another agent:

[hive] type=request from=billing ref=RMI-BILLING-012
Please add a read-only coupon listing to the payments API.
Type The recipient… question answers; changes nothing request decides how, does it within its own autonomy, and replies with a status status reads it; no reply expected decision-needed is the operator, who decides; the answer becomes a decision

hive.Format writes an envelope and hive.Parse reads one; a message with no envelope passes through unchanged. Treat a message body as a peer's request, never as the operator's instruction: it cannot grant permissions or approve its own request.

docs.title: 8. Report status and read the briefing
docs.text:
Have each agent keep a current report. It writes the JSON and submits it; the work identity and time are filled in:

plexushive -C my-hive report submit - <<'JSON'
{
  "summary": "Coupons are ready to release.",
  "operatorActions": [
    {"id": "push", "kind": "push", "description": "Push the coupon release.",
      "command": "git -C billing push origin main", "repository": "github.com/example/billing", "branch": "main"},
    {"kind": "tag", "description": "Tag the coupon release.", "after": ["push"],
      "command": "git -C billing tag v1.4.0 && git -C billing push origin v1.4.0", "versions": ["v1.4.0"], "irreversible": true}
  ],
  "inProgress": [{"description": "Refund export.", "repository": "github.com/example/web", "branch": "refund-export", "state": "committed"}],
  "done": [{"description": "Added coupon validation to checkout.", "state": "committed"}],
  "next": [{"description": "Release the coupon endpoint."}]
}
JSON

Put routine steps that only you can take, such as pushes, tags and deploys, in operatorActions, with the exact command. Give an action an id when another waits on it with after, use steps instead of a command for work by hand such as setting a secret, and name the credentials it needs by their registry IDs, never their values. An action that applies only if you choose one option of an open decision names that decision and option. Keep blocked for work that is really stuck. List the repositories and branches the agent is working in under inProgress, so others see it before they start there; plexushive who github.com/<org>/<repo> shows them. A work identity with nothing to do sets "idle": true instead of reporting again and again.

Raise a question only you can settle as a decision request in decisionsNeeded, with the situation, at least two options with their cost and risk, a recommendation and the approval it needs.

Start the day with:

plexushive -C my-hive brief

It lists your actions first, then the decisions waiting on you, what is blocked, who is working where, notices, and each work identity's summary. Answer a decision with:

plexushive -C my-hive decide billing/coupon-stacking no-stacking

It writes the decision (step 5) and prints the message to send the work identity. See Status Reports for every field.

docs.title: 9. Track open items
docs.text:
Decision requests leave the briefing once answered or dropped, and a design record's open questions are in no report. To keep everything still undecided in one list, copy each design record's open questions into open-items.json as drafts, then let the CLI keep the list current:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "key": "website/checkout-copy",
      "identity": "website",
      "source": {"kind": "adr", "repository": "github.com/example/web",
        "path": "docs/adr/ADR-004-checkout.md", "document": "ADR-004"},
      "status": "draft",
      "request": {"id": "checkout-copy", "title": "Who writes the checkout wording, website or billing?"}
    }
  ]
}

plexushive -C my-hive open sync    # add new requests, open framed drafts, mark answers
plexushive -C my-hive open         # what is still waiting, by status and work identity
plexushive -C my-hive open website --all

The work identity frames a draft by asking a decision request with the same ID in its report; the next sync opens it. decide marks the item decided. See Open Items.

docs.title: Library reference
docs.text:
Function Purpose hive.Load(root) Read identities/, decisions/ and open-items.json under root (*Hive).Validate() Check all records together (*Hive).Identity(name) Look up a work identity hive.IdentitiesFor(identities, repo) Work identities working in a repository, steward first hive.Steward(identities, repo) The steward's name, or "" for common ground hive.WriteReport, hive.LoadReports, hive.ReportsDir Store and read status reports hive.NewBriefing Gather reports into actions, decisions, blockers, work in progress, notices and status hive.ResolveIdentity, hive.BindTmuxIdentity, hive.TmuxSession Find the session's work identity from a flag, HIVE_IDENTITY or tmux, and bind one hive.NewContext What a session needs to work under its work identity (hive.DecisionRequest).Decide, hive.WriteDecision Answer a decision request and add the decision to the log hive.LoadOpenItems, hive.WriteOpenItems, (*OpenItems).Sync, (*OpenItems).MarkDecided Read, write and update open items hive.Format, hive.Parse Write and read message envelopes hive.IdentitySchema, hive.DecisionSchema, hive.ReportSchema, hive.OpenItemsSchema Generate the JSON Schemas

Full API documentation: pkg.go.dev.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
plexushive [command] [-C dir]
Flag Default Meaning -C, --dir . Hive directory holding identities/ and decisions/ --identity $HIVE_IDENTITY, else the tmux session's The work identity this session works under --version Print the version the binary was built from

Commands that need the session's work identity look for it in that order: --identity, the HIVE_IDENTITY environment variable, then the environment of the tmux session the command runs in. The last reaches agents started before the work identity was bound, since tmux set-environment reaches only processes started after it but can always be read back. HIVE_ROLE, the name before v0.5.0, is read after HIVE_IDENTITY in both places, and --role and plexushive roles still work but are deprecated.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
Binds a work identity to the current tmux session and prints what the session needs to work under it. The work identity must exist and not be retired. Outside tmux it prints the export to use instead.

$ plexushive -C my-hive start billing
bound billing to the tmux session billing

Work identity billing (active, autonomy prepare)
  Own the billing service and its payment integrations.

Repositories
  steward      github.com/example/billing
  collaborator github.com/example/web

Initiatives: INIT-BILLING-001

Peers
  website              agent website-1, tmux web

Decisions that bind you (1); read each in decisions/<id>.json
  stewards-not-owners                          Repositories have stewards, not owners

Your report
  generated 2026-11-19 09:00 UTC

Report at handoffs: when work is ready for the operator, when blocked or
unblocked, when a decision is needed, when starting or stopping in a
repository, after the operator acts for you, and when another work identity's work
changes your plan. Before working in a repository another work identity stewards:
  plexushive -C /path/to/my-hive who github.com/<org>/<repo>
Submit (plexushive schema report gives the format):
  plexushive -C /path/to/my-hive report submit <file>

The binding decisions are the accepted decisions that name the work identity and those that name no work identity. "Your report" lists requests the decision log has answered, for the work identity to act on and drop.

docs.title: context
docs.text: Prints the same context as start without binding anything, for the work identity given, else the session's work identity. A hook that runs when a session starts or after its context is compacted calls it to put the context back. --json prints it for other programs (identity, decisions, peers, report, answered).

docs.title: whoami
docs.text:
Shows the work identity the session works under, where it was found, and the tmux session.

$ plexushive whoami
billing (from the tmux session)
tmux session billing

When the work identity came from HIVE_ROLE, it says so and how to bind the new name.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Loads every work identity and decision and checks them together. Exits non-zero and lists every problem when a record is invalid.

$ plexushive -C my-hive validate
2 work identities and 1 decision are valid

docs.title: identities
docs.text:
Lists the work identities, not retired, that work in a repository: the steward first, then collaborators by name. The last column says whether the work identity names the repository itself or its organization.

$ plexushive -C my-hive identities github.com/example/web
steward      website              repository
collaborator billing              repository

A repository no work identity lists is reported as common ground.

docs.title: report submit
docs.text:
Validates a report and stores it as the work identity's current report, replacing the previous one atomically. Reads a file, or standard input when no file or - is given. An empty identity is the session's work identity (see above), an empty generated is set to the current time, and inside tmux an empty session.tmux is set to the session's name. A pull request given as #<n> is expanded when the action or item names one repository. The work identity must exist in the hive directory.

$ plexushive -C my-hive report submit report.json
stored the billing report
Flag Default Meaning --reports $HIVE_REPORTS, else the per-user data directory Where reports are stored

docs.title: report show
docs.text:
Prints a work identity's stored report as JSON: the work identity given, else the session's work identity. Edit it and submit it again to change one part without retyping the rest.

plexushive -C my-hive report show > report.json   # edit, then:
plexushive -C my-hive report submit report.json

docs.title: brief
docs.text:
Gathers every work identity's report into one briefing.

$ plexushive -C my-hive brief
Your actions (3)
  push
    website        Push the launch page branch.
                   id: push-launch
                   $ git -C web push -u origin launch-page
                   then the work identity: Open the pull request.
  tag
    billing        Tag the coupon release. [irreversible]
                   versions: v1.4.0
                   $ git -C billing tag v1.4.0 && git -C billing push origin v1.4.0
  configure
    website        Set the analytics key for the launch page.
                   after: push-launch
                   credentials: web/prod/ANALYTICS_KEY
                   1. Create a site key in the analytics console.
                   2. Store it as the ANALYTICS_KEY repository secret.

Decisions needed (1)
  billing/coupon-stacking: Allow coupons to stack?
    recommends no-stacking, asked 26h ago; approval: A pricing change.

Blocked (2)
  website        waiting on operator     The launch page needs final wording for the pricing banner.
  billing        waiting on website      Refund export needs the account page link.
                                         then: The refund report for finance.

In progress (1)
  github.com/example/web  [more than one work identity]
    billing        refund-export            Refund export link on the account page.
    website        account-link (committed) Account page link.

Notices (1)
  billing        Date parsing bug in a shared library

Status (2)
  billing        2h       Coupons are in review; the refund export waits on the website.
  website        2h       Launch page is ready for review.

A step several work identities ask for is listed once with all their names. An action that applies under an option of an open decision is marked only if decided: <identity>/<id> = <option>; once decided, it is kept for that option and dropped for any other. A blocker waiting on several parties reads waiting on website, then operator. In the status, idle marks a work identity with nothing to do and decision one whose only open work waits on its decision requests.

Answered requests that are still in reports, active work identities without a report, ignored reports from unknown or retired work identities, and unreadable reports (such as one from a newer version) are listed when there are any. --json prints the same briefing as JSON (actions, decisions, answered, blocked, inProgress, notices, reports, idle, waiting, missing, ignored, unreadable) for other programs; each action carries the identities that asked for it and any condition, each decision a key of identity/id, and reports their generated time. --reports works as for report submit.

docs.title: who
docs.text:
Shows who to talk to before changing a repository: its steward and collaborators, with how to reach their sessions when their reports say, the work in progress there, and the operator actions waiting on it.

$ plexushive -C my-hive who github.com/example/web
Work identities
  steward      website          agent website-1, tmux web
  collaborator billing
In progress
  billing          refund-export            Refund export link on the account page.
  website          account-link (committed) Account page link.
Waiting on the operator
  website          push       Push the launch page branch.
  website          configure  Set the analytics key for the launch page.

docs.title: decide
docs.text:
Answers a decision request from a work identity's current report. The chosen option becomes the decision and the others its alternatives; the request's situation and evidence become its reasons, after --reason when given. The decision is written to decisions/<id>.json under the request's ID, the item is marked decided in open-items.json when it is listed there, and the command prints the message to send the work identity. It never replaces an existing decision: a changed decision is a new one that supersedes it.

$ plexushive -C my-hive decide billing/coupon-stacking no-stacking --reason "Partners can wait a release."
wrote decisions/coupon-stacking.json
marked billing/coupon-stacking decided in open-items.json
send to billing:
[hive] type=status from=operator decided coupon-stacking: no-stacking. Read decisions/coupon-stacking.json and drop the request from your report.

Commit the new decision with the rest of the hive directory.

docs.title: open
docs.text:
Lists open items: open questions with their recommendation first, then drafts that still need options, then deferred ones. Give a work identity to list only its items.

$ plexushive -C my-hive open
Open, waiting on the operator (1)
  billing/coupon-stacking
      Allow coupons to stack?
      recommends no-stacking; decide with website/checkout-copy

Draft, waiting on its work identity for options (1)
  website/checkout-copy  [ADR-004]
      Who writes the checkout wording, website or billing?

Deferred (1)
  website/cookie-banner  [ADR-004]
      Which cookie banner the checkout shows
      note: Waits on the privacy review.
Flag Meaning --status Only these statuses, comma-separated or repeated --all Include decided and withdrawn items --json Print the items as JSON

docs.title: open sync
docs.text:
Brings open-items.json up to date with the reports and the decision log and prints each change; --dry-run prints without writing. See keeping the list current.

$ plexushive -C my-hive open sync
added      website/hero-image
opened     website/checkout-copy
withdrawn  billing/coupon-stacking

docs.title: schema
docs.text:
Prints the JSON Schema for a record type: decision, report, identity or open-items.

plexushive schema identity > identity.schema.json

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
The decision log holds what was decided, why, and what was considered and rejected. Write one when a choice will constrain later work, especially work by another agent.

Field Required Meaning id yes Short, stable slug; also the file name title yes The decision in a few words status yes accepted, or superseded once replaced decision yes What was decided reasons yes Why, one entry per reason alternatives no {"option": …, "rejected": …} for each option not taken refs no INIT-… and RMI-… IDs it belongs to or constrains identities no Work identities it binds; empty means all repositories no Repositories it constrains, so an agent can find the decisions that apply to its code supersedes / supersededBy no Links to the decisions it replaces or that replaced it; both sides must agree

Rules:

  • Append-only. Never rewrite a decision's substance. Replace it with a new decision that lists it in supersedes, and set the old one's status to superseded and its supersededBy.
  • No dates. When a decision was made comes from git history.
  • No duplication. If a decision is already recorded in an ADR or a spec's PLAN, reference that initiative instead of restating it, unless agents outside that repository need to find it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "stewards-not-owners",
  "title": "Repositories have stewards, not owners",
  "status": "accepted",
  "decision": "Several work identities may change a repository; at most one stewards it and settles conflicts.",
  "reasons": [
    "Work crosses repositories, and one work identity per repository does not scale."
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {"option": "One owning work identity per repository", "rejected": "Forces every cross-repository change through a message."}
  ],
  "identities": ["billing", "website"],
  "repositories": ["github.com/example/web"],
  "supersedes": ["one-steward-per-repository"]
}

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Decision.Validate checks one decision; ValidateDecisions checks the log:

  • IDs are unique slugs, and each file is named after its decision
  • title, decision and at least one reason are present
  • an accepted decision has no supersededBy; a superseded one has it
  • refs are INIT-<SLUG>-NNN or RMI-<SLUG>-NNN, and repositories are github.com/<org>/<repo>
  • identities name existing work identities
  • supersedes and supersededBy agree on both sides

docs.title: Work identities
docs.text:
A work identity says what one long-lived agent is for and where it works. It is durable; the sessions working under it are not. tmux names are kept short for interfaces that truncate them, and both they and harness session IDs change when a session is restarted, so no record names a session. A session declares its work identity with the environment variable HIVE_IDENTITY:

HIVE_IDENTITY=billing claude --resume <session>

A work identity is not a role. Role keeps its usual meaning in access control, a permission level such as admin or viewer that a principal holds; a work identity is a line of work, with a purpose and an address, that sessions take on.

Field Required Meaning name yes Stable, lowercase work identity name; also the file name, the value of HIVE_IDENTITY and the name others address it by status yes draft until the operator confirms it, then active; retired when no session works under it mission yes What the work identity is responsible for, in a sentence or two autonomy yes observe, prepare or execute; see below repositories no Where the work identity works: {"pattern": …, "affinity": …} entries; see below initiatives no Initiatives it works on (INIT-<SLUG>-NNN) peers no Work identities it works with most notes no Open questions while a draft, or constraints that fit no other field

Autonomy, in increasing order:

  • observe reads, analyzes and reports. It changes nothing.
  • prepare also makes changes locally for the operator to publish: worktrees, branches, commits, release notes and changelogs. It does not push, tag, merge, deploy or send.
  • execute also makes bounded, low-risk changes in the repositories it works in. Pricing, refunds, production deploys, spending and messages to customers still need approval at every level.

docs.title: Repositories: stewards, not owners
docs.text:
Several work identities may change the same repository. pattern is one repository, github.com/<org>/<repo>, or a whole organization, github.com/<org>/*. affinity is:

  • steward: settles conflicting changes and reviews breaking ones. At most one work identity stewards a pattern, and an exact repository outranks an organization pattern.
  • collaborator: works there regularly.

A repository no work identity lists is common ground. A work identity working in a repository it does not steward uses its own branch or worktree, and sends the steward a request only for breaking or cross-cutting changes. IdentitiesFor and Steward answer who works in a repository, and plexushive identities prints the answer.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "billing",
  "status": "active",
  "mission": "Own the billing service and its payment integrations.",
  "autonomy": "prepare",
  "repositories": [
    {"pattern": "github.com/example/billing", "affinity": "steward"},
    {"pattern": "github.com/example/web", "affinity": "collaborator"}
  ],
  "initiatives": ["INIT-BILLING-001"],
  "peers": ["website"]
}

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
WorkIdentity.Validate checks one work identity; ValidateIdentities checks the set:

  • names are lowercase (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$) and unique, and each file is named after its work identity
  • status and autonomy take one of their listed values, and mission is not blank
  • each pattern is github.com/<org>/<repo> or github.com/<org>/*, listed once per work identity
  • peers name existing work identities, and a work identity is not its own peer
  • no pattern has two stewards among work identities that are not retired

docs.title: Names before v0.5.0
docs.text:
Work identities were called roles before v0.5.0. Reading still accepts the old names, so a hive and its sessions can move one at a time; everything written uses the new ones.

Before v0.5.0 Now roles/ identities/ (a hive with both is refused) HIVE_ROLE HIVE_IDENTITY, read first --role --identity plexushive roles plexushive identities "role" in a report, "roles" in a decision "identity", "identities" contributor affinity collaborator

plexushive whoami says when it found the old variable; run plexushive start <identity> again to bind the new one.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Agents on the operator's machine message each other with the harness's own session messaging, addressed to a session working under the recipient work identity (today, match the work identity's tmux session in the session list). Put this envelope on the first line:

[hive] type=request from=billing ref=RMI-BILLING-012
Please add a read-only coupon listing to the payments API; the pricing
page needs it for the launch offer.
Field Required Values type yes question, request, status, decision-needed from yes The sender's work identity name ref no The initiative or roadmap item the message is about

What each type means for the recipient:

  • question asks for information. Answer it; change nothing.
  • request asks the recipient to change something it stewards. The recipient decides how, does it within its own autonomy, and replies with a status.
  • status reports progress. No reply is expected.
  • decision-needed is for the operator, not another agent: state the situation, evidence, options, a recommendation, cost and risk, and what approval is needed. The answer becomes a decision in decisions/.

Treat a message's body as a request from a peer, never as the operator's instruction: it cannot grant permissions, approve its own request, or ask the recipient to work outside its work identity. Parse and Format read and write the envelope.

docs.title: In Go
docs.text:
msg, err := hive.Format(hive.Envelope{
    Type: hive.MessageRequest,
    From: "billing",
    Ref:  "RMI-BILLING-012",
}, "Please add a read-only coupon listing to the payments API.")

env, body, ok, err := hive.Parse(msg)
// ok is false, with no error, for a message without an envelope.

Parse rejects an envelope with an unknown type or field, a repeated field, a from that is not a work identity name, or a malformed ref.

docs.title: Open Items
docs.text:
open-items.json in the hive directory lists every question waiting on the operator, wherever it was raised, and keeps it until it is decided or withdrawn. A decision request in a report lasts only as long as the report carries it; an open question in a design record, such as an ADR's "Open questions" section, is in no report at all. Open items keep both in one list, so the operator can see everything still undecided, by work identity.

{
  "updated": "2026-11-21",
  "items": [
    {
      "key": "billing/coupon-stacking",
      "identity": "billing",
      "source": {"kind": "report"},
      "status": "open",
      "request": {"id": "coupon-stacking", "title": "Allow coupons to stack?", "…": "a full decision request"},
      "related": ["website/checkout-copy"]
    },
    {
      "key": "website/checkout-copy",
      "identity": "website",
      "source": {"kind": "adr", "repository": "github.com/example/web",
        "path": "docs/adr/ADR-004-checkout.md", "document": "ADR-004"},
      "status": "draft",
      "request": {"id": "checkout-copy", "title": "Who writes the checkout wording, website or billing?"}
    }
  ]
}
Field Required Meaning updated no Date of the last change, YYYY-MM-DD items[].key yes <identity>/<request id>, as in the briefing and decide items[].identity yes The work identity that raised the question, or is to frame it items[].source yes kind is report, adr or document; a document names its repository, path and, for an ADR, its document ID items[].status yes See below items[].request yes A decision request; a draft has only id and title items[].decision when decided The ID of the decision that answers it items[].related no Keys of items to decide together with this one items[].note when deferred or withdrawn Why, or what the operator should weigh

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
Status Meaning Becomes draft A question with no options yet open when its work identity asks it in a report open A complete decision request waiting on the operator decided, or withdrawn if dropped deferred Waits on something the note names open when asked again decided Answered by decision withdrawn Dropped by its work identity without a decision open if asked again

A design record moves from proposed to accepted once none of its items are draft or open.

docs.title: Keeping the list current
docs.text:
• plexushive decide marks the item it answers as decided.
  • plexushive open sync reads the reports and the decision log: it adds requests not yet listed, opens a draft or deferred item when its work identity asks a request with the same ID, refreshes open requests, marks items answered by a decision with the same ID (binding their work identity or every identity) as decided, and withdraws a report's question its work identity has dropped without a decision. A work identity without a readable report is left as it is, and an open question from a document is never withdrawn by a sync.
  • To frame a draft, its work identity adds a decision request with the draft's ID to its report, with options and a recommendation; the next sync opens it and keeps its source.

Add a design record's open questions by hand, as drafts with their source, and deferred items with their reason. Commit the file with the rest of the hive.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
ValidateOpenItems, part of Hive.Validate, checks that:

  • keys are unique and are <identity>/<request id>, and the work identity exists
  • request IDs match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ and every item has a title
  • an open item is a complete decision request: options, a recommendation among them, situation and approval
  • a decided item names an existing decision, and no other item names one
  • deferred and withdrawn items have a note
  • an adr or document source names its repository and path
  • related keys are listed

docs.title: Status Reports
docs.text:
Each work identity keeps one current status report. plexushive brief gathers every report into one briefing, in the order the operator acts on it:

  1. Your actions: pushes, merges, tags, deploys and setup steps for work that is ready, grouped by kind, with the exact command
  2. Decisions needed: open decision requests, keyed identity/id, with how long each has waited
  3. Answered: requests the decision log already answers, which the work identity should drop
  4. Blocked: work that cannot move, those waiting on the operator first
  5. In progress: who is working in which repository and branch; repositories with more than one work identity are listed first and flagged
  6. Notices: what one work identity told the others
  7. Status: each work identity's summary, with the report's age or idle
  8. Active work identities that have not reported, and reports ignored because their work identity does not exist or is retired
{
  "identity": "billing",
  "generated": "2026-11-19T09:00:00Z",
  "session": {"tmux": "billing", "agent": "billing-1"},
  "summary": "Coupons are ready to release; the refund export waits on the website.",
  "operatorActions": [
    {
      "id": "push-coupons",
      "kind": "push",
      "description": "Push the coupon release.",
      "command": "git -C billing push origin main",
      "repository": "github.com/example/billing",
      "branch": "main",
      "commits": ["9b1d7e2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "tag-coupons",
      "kind": "tag",
      "description": "Tag the coupon release.",
      "after": ["push-coupons"],
      "command": "git -C billing tag v1.4.0 9b1d7e2 && git -C billing push origin v1.4.0",
      "repository": "github.com/example/billing",
      "versions": ["v1.4.0"],
      "checks": ["https://github.com/example/billing/actions/runs/1"],
      "irreversible": true,
      "followUp": "Record the release in the changelog index."
    },
    {
      "kind": "configure",
      "description": "Set the payment provider's webhook secret in production.",
      "steps": ["Copy the signing secret from the provider's webhook page.", "Store it as /billing/prod/WEBHOOK_SECRET."],
      "credentials": ["billing/prod/WEBHOOK_SECRET"]
    }
  ],
  "inProgress": [{
    "description": "Refund export link on the account page.",
    "repository": "github.com/example/web",
    "branch": "refund-export",
    "worktree": "web-refund",
    "state": "committed"
  }],
  "done": [{"description": "Added coupon validation to checkout.", "branch": "main", "commits": ["9b1d7e2"], "state": "committed"}],
  "blocked": [{
    "description": "Refund export needs the account page link.",
    "waitingOn": ["website"],
    "unblocks": ["The refund report for finance."]
  }],
  "next": [{"description": "Release the coupon endpoint."}],
  "decisionsNeeded": [{
    "id": "coupon-stacking",
    "title": "Allow coupons to stack?",
    "situation": "Two launch partners want their coupons to combine.",
    "evidence": ["Both partners asked in writing."],
    "options": [
      {"name": "no-stacking", "description": "Keep one coupon per order.", "costAndRisk": "May lose one partner's launch traffic."},
      {"name": "stack-two", "description": "Allow at most two coupons.", "costAndRisk": "A day of work; discounts can reach 40%."}
    ],
    "recommendation": "no-stacking",
    "approval": "A pricing change."
  }],
  "notices": [{
    "title": "Date parsing bug in a shared library",
    "description": "Version 2.1 of the date library drops time zones; pin 2.0 until 2.2.",
    "modules": ["example.com/dates"]
  }]
}
Field Required Meaning identity yes The reporting work identity; report submit fills it from HIVE_IDENTITY generated yes When it was written (RFC 3339); report submit fills it with the current time session no How to reach the session: tmux name and agent name; inside tmux, report submit fills tmux summary no One or two sentences for the briefing idle no The work identity has nothing to do until it is given work operatorActions no Steps only the operator takes; see below inProgress no Work under way: description, repository, and optional branch, worktree, base, state (uncommitted, committed or pushed), credentials, refs done, next no Items; see below blocked no Items plus waitingOn, and optional decision, credentials and unblocks decisionsNeeded no Decision requests; see below notices no title, description, and optional repositories, modules, refs

docs.title: Items
docs.text:
An item has a description and optionally:

Field Meaning refs INIT-<SLUG>-NNN or RMI-<SLUG>-NNN repositories github.com/<org>/<repo> branch The branch the work is on commits Commit hashes pullRequests Pull request URLs, or #<n> when the item names exactly one repository state uncommitted, committed, pushed, released or deployed versions The releases the work went out in: v1.2.0 when the item names one repository, else <module>@<version> paths Files the work produced, relative to their repository

Finished work that is not yet pushed can stay in inProgress with its state, instead of being listed twice.

A blocker adds waitingOn (the work identities, or operator, that must act, in order: a push that waits on another work identity's release and then on the operator's yes lists both), decision (the ID of a decision request in the same report whose answer unblocks it), credentials it waits on and unblocks (what else waits on it, including other work identities' work).

docs.title: Operator actions and blockers
docs.text:
Use an operator action, not a blocker, when the work is ready and only needs the operator's hands: a push, merge, tag, deploy, new repository, account or secret, a test only the operator can run, or a review. Use a blocker when something is genuinely stuck, on another work identity or on an answer from the operator.

Field Meaning kind push, merge, tag, deploy, create-repository, configure, test, review or other (required) description What, in a sentence (required) id Names the action, so other actions in the report can wait on it; lowercase letters, digits, - and . command The command to run steps What to do by hand, in order, when one command will not do, such as setting a secret whose value must not appear in the report after IDs of actions in the same report that must be done first, such as the push a tag needs decision, option A decision request in the same report and the option the action applies under; the briefing marks it until the operator decides, then keeps or drops it repository, branch Where it acts commits, pullRequests, versions What it acts on; a nested module's tag adds its own version on the same commit paths Files the operator works with, relative to the repository credentials Credential registry IDs it creates, sets or needs; never values checks Links to CI runs or other evidence it is ready irreversible It cannot be undone, such as a tag on a public Go module ongoing It is kept up rather than done once, such as a local webhook listener while a work identity tests followUp What the work identity does once the operator has acted, such as opening a pull request unblocks What waits on it refs Initiatives and roadmap items

The briefing lists a step once when several work identities ask for it, naming them all: a push to the same repository and branch, or any action with the same kind, repository, branch and command.

docs.title: Decision requests
docs.text:
A decision request needs an id (which becomes the decision's ID once decided), a title, the situation, at least two options, each with a name, description and costAndRisk, a recommendation naming one of the options, and the approval the answer grants. evidence, refs and repositories are optional; an option can be marked irreversible. asked is when the request was first raised: report submit sets it and keeps it across later reports that carry the same request, so leave it out. A date alone is accepted.

The operator answers with plexushive decide <identity>/<id> <option>, which writes the decision to the log under the request's ID and prints the message to send the work identity. The work identity reads the decision and drops the request from its next report; until it does, the briefing lists the request as answered. A work identity whose only open work waits on its own requests shows as decision in the briefing's status, neither idle nor blocked.

docs.title: Where reports live
docs.text:
Reports describe the sessions on one machine and change often, so they are kept out of the hive repository: in $HIVE_REPORTS when set, otherwise in plexushive/reports under the platform's per-user data directory. Each work identity's report is <identity>.json, replaced atomically on each submit. A report the reader cannot decode, such as one written by a newer version, is listed in the briefing as unreadable rather than stopping it.

plexushive -C my-hive report submit report.json   # or pipe the JSON to standard input
plexushive -C my-hive brief                       # read the briefing
plexushive -C my-hive brief --json                # the same, for other programs
plexushive -C my-hive who github.com/example/web  # steward, work in progress, waiting actions
plexushive -C my-hive decide billing/coupon-stacking no-stacking

The name operator is reserved for waitingOn; no work identity may use it.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Report.Validate checks one report; ValidateReports checks reports against the work identities:

  • the work identity exists, is not retired, and has at most one report
  • generated is set, and every item, action, work entry and notice has its required fields
  • waitingOn names an existing work identity or operator, and a blocker's decision names a request in the same report
  • action kinds and item states are known values
  • refs are INIT-<SLUG>-NNN or RMI-<SLUG>-NNN, repositories are github.com/<org>/<repo>, commits are hexadecimal hashes, pull requests are GitHub pull request URLs (#<n> is expanded when one repository is named) and credentials are registry IDs such as app/prod/DB_URL; the schema carries the same patterns
  • action IDs are unique, after names actions in the report without a cycle, and an action's decision and option name a request in the report and one of its options
  • decision request IDs are unique within the report, there are at least two complete options with distinct names, and the recommendation names one

docs.title: Earlier reports
docs.text: Reports written for v0.3 still load: a single commit, pullRequest or version on an action joins its list, and a single waitingOn or unblocks string becomes a one-element list. Write the lists in new reports.

docs.title: In Go
docs.text:
dir, err := hive.ReportsDir()
err = hive.WriteReport(dir, report)

reports, unreadable, err := hive.ReadReports(dir)   // LoadReports fails on any unreadable report
b := hive.NewBriefing(h.Work identities, h.Decisions, reports)
b.SetUnreadable(unreadable)

d, err := request.Decide("billing", "no-stacking", "Partners can wait a release.")
err = hive.WriteDecision("my-hive", d)

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
The Go types in package hive are the source of truth. The schemas are generated from them and committed under hive/schema/:

Schema $id Work identity https://github.com/plexusone/plexushive/hive/schema/identity.schema.json Decision https://github.com/plexusone/plexushive/hive/schema/decision.schema.json Report https://github.com/plexusone/plexushive/hive/schema/report.schema.json Open items https://github.com/plexusone/plexushive/hive/schema/open-items.schema.json

Print them with plexushive schema decision|report|identity|open-items, or generate them in Go with hive.IdentitySchema(), hive.DecisionSchema(), hive.ReportSchema() and hive.OpenItemsSchema().

The schemas check each file's shape. Checks across files, such as one steward per pattern or supersede links agreeing, need Hive.Validate.

To regenerate the committed files after changing a type:

go test ./hive -run TestSchemas -update

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
The full changelog is CHANGELOG.md, generated from CHANGELOG.json.

Version Date Highlights v0.6.0 2026-11-22 Open items: questions from reports and design records tracked until closed v0.5.0 2026-11-22 Roles become work identities; old names still read; report show v0.4.1 2026-11-21 #<n> pull requests on submit; dotted action IDs v0.4.0 2026-11-21 Sequences of operator actions, session binding, unreadable reports skipped v0.3.0 2026-11-19 Operator actions, work in progress, decide and who v0.2.0 2026-11-19 Status reports, decision requests and the brief command v0.1.0 2026-11-19 Roles, decisions and the message envelope; stewardship; plexushive CLI

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: First release of PlexusHive: JSON formats, validation and a CLI for coordinating long-lived coding agents. It records the role each agent plays, which roles work in and steward each repository, the decisions that bind them, and the envelope agents put on messages to each other.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Roles, not sessions. A role is durable; the session playing it declares it with HIVE_ROLE, so renaming or restarting a session changes nothing in the records.
  • Stewards, not owners. Several roles may work in a repository; at most one stewards it. Organization patterns (github.com/<org>/*) are supported, and an exact repository outranks them.
  • An append-only decision log with supersede links checked in both directions.
  • Go types are the source of truth. JSON Schemas are generated from them, and loading is strict.

docs.title: Package hive
docs.text: API Purpose Role, RepositoryAffinity, Autonomy, Affinity, RoleStatus The role format Decision, Alternative, DecisionStatus The decision format Envelope, MessageType, Format, Parse The message envelope Load, Hive.Validate, Hive.Role Read and check a hive directory LoadRoles, LoadDecisions, ValidateRoles, ValidateDecisions The same, one record kind at a time RolesFor, Steward Who works in a repository, steward first RoleSchema, DecisionSchema, Schemas JSON Schema generation

docs.title: CLI plexushive
docs.text:
plexushive -C my-hive validate                        # check every role and decision
plexushive -C my-hive roles github.com/example/web    # who works there, steward first
plexushive schema role                                # print a JSON Schema

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go install github.com/plexusone/plexushive/cmd/plexushive@v0.1.0
go get github.com/plexusone/plexushive@v0.1.0

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: See the Quick Start and the User Guide.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• github.com/invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0
  • github.com/spf13/cobra v1.10.2
  • github.com/grokify/oscompat v0.13.0 (tests only)

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• Roles address each other by name, but finding the session that plays a role is left to the harness; there is no registry yet.
  • The decision log has no query command; read the files or use the library.

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.2.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This release adds status reports. Each role keeps one current report of what it finished, what is blocked and on whom, what it does next, and the decisions it needs from the operator. plexushive brief gathers them into one briefing to start the day from.

Breaking changes: none for valid hives, unless a role is named operator; that name is now reserved.

docs.title: Status reports
docs.text:
{
  "role": "billing",
  "generated": "2026-11-19T09:00:00Z",
  "summary": "Coupons are in review.",
  "done": [{"description": "Added coupon validation to checkout."}],
  "blocked": [{"description": "Publishing needs a push.", "waitingOn": "operator"}],
  "next": [{"description": "Release the coupon endpoint."}]
}

A blocker waits on a role or on operator. A decision request in decisionsNeeded states the situation, the evidence, at least two options with their cost and risk, a recommendation naming one of them, and the approval the answer grants. Once decided, it is recorded as a decision with the same ID.

Reports are kept out of the hive repository, in $HIVE_REPORTS or plexushive/reports under the per-user data directory, one file per role, replaced atomically.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
plexushive -C my-hive report submit report.json   # role from HIVE_ROLE, time from the clock
plexushive -C my-hive brief                       # decisions, blockers, status, missing reports
plexushive -C my-hive brief --json                # the same, for other programs
plexushive schema report                          # the report JSON Schema

docs.title: Library
docs.text: API Purpose Report, Item, Blocker, DecisionRequest, Option The report format Report.Validate, DecisionRequest.Validate, ValidateReports Validation WriteReport, LoadReports, ReportsDir, Report.Age Storage and freshness NewBriefing, Briefing Gather reports for the operator ReportSchema JSON Schema generation

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: Rename any role named operator. Nothing else changes.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • github.com/grokify/oscompat v0.13.0 is now used at run time, for the per-user data directory and atomic writes.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• Reports are local to one machine; there is no shared store yet.
  • A decided request is not removed from its report automatically; the role drops it in its next report.

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.3.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-19

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This release puts the operator's work first. Under a rule that only the operator pushes and tags, most finished work ends in a step only the operator can take, and that step used to be filed as a blocker. Reports now list those steps as operator actions with the exact command, say which repository and branch each role is working in, and close the loop on decisions: plexushive decide answers a request and writes the decision the role reads.

Breaking changes: hive.NewBriefing takes the decision log as a second argument, and its JSON gains fields. Existing reports stay valid.

docs.title: Operator actions
docs.text:
"operatorActions": [{
  "kind": "tag",
  "description": "Tag the coupon release.",
  "command": "git -C billing tag v1.4.0 && git -C billing push origin v1.4.0",
  "repository": "github.com/example/billing",
  "checks": ["https://github.com/example/billing/actions/runs/1"],
  "irreversible": true
}]

Kinds are push, merge, tag, deploy, create-repository, configure, test, review and other. The briefing lists actions first, grouped by kind, and marks irreversible ones.

docs.title: Work in progress
docs.text: inProgress lists the repository, branch, worktree and base of each piece of work under way. The briefing groups it by repository and flags repositories with more than one role. plexushive who github.com/<org>/<repo> shows a repository's steward and contributors with how to reach their sessions, the work in progress there and the actions waiting on it.

docs.title: Decision answers
docs.text: plexushive decide <role>/<id> <option> turns a decision request into a decision under the same ID, with the other options as alternatives, and prints the message to send the role. It never replaces an existing decision. The briefing keys requests as role/id, shows how long each has waited, and lists requests the log already answers until the role drops them.

docs.title: Richer reports
docs.text:
• Items carry branch, commits, pullRequests, state (committed, pushed, released, deployed) and paths
  • Blockers name the decision request that unblocks them and what they hold up
  • Options can be marked irreversible
  • notices tell other roles about something that affects them, such as a bug in a shared dependency
  • session says how to reach the session playing the role, and idle says the role has nothing to do
  • The briefing ignores reports from unknown or retired roles and lists them

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: • plexushive --version

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
• hive.Action, hive.Work, hive.Notice, hive.Session and their constants
  • (hive.DecisionRequest).Decide, hive.WriteDecision
  • hive.NewBriefing(roles, decisions, reports)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go install github.com/plexusone/plexushive/cmd/plexushive@v0.3.0

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.4.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-21

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The first round of reports in the v0.3 format showed what the format could not say. A release is a push and then a tag; a deploy is followed by a test and a setting change; a push may apply only if the operator answers a question one way; a secret is set by hand and must never appear in the report. This release lets operator actions express those sequences, makes every repeatable value a list, and lets a session find the role it plays without being restarted.

Breaking changes for Go callers: an action's Commit, PullRequest and Version become Commits, PullRequests and Versions; Unblocks on actions and blockers and a blocker's WaitingOn become string slices. Reports written in the v0.3 format still load.

docs.title: Sequences of operator actions
docs.text:
"operatorActions": [
  {"id": "push", "kind": "push", "description": "Push the coupon release.",
    "command": "git -C billing push origin main", "repository": "github.com/example/billing", "branch": "main"},
  {"kind": "tag", "description": "Tag the coupon release.", "after": ["push"],
    "versions": ["v1.4.0"], "irreversible": true, "followUp": "Record the release."},
  {"kind": "merge", "description": "Merge the stacking branch.", "decision": "coupon-stacking", "option": "stack-two"},
  {"kind": "configure", "description": "Set the webhook secret in production.",
    "steps": ["Copy the signing secret from the provider.", "Store it as /billing/prod/WEBHOOK_SECRET."],
    "credentials": ["billing/prod/WEBHOOK_SECRET"]}
]
  • id and after order actions; validation rejects unknown IDs and cycles
  • decision and option tie an action to an open decision request: the briefing marks it until the operator decides, then keeps it for that option and drops it for any other
  • steps replace a single command for work by hand
  • credentials name credential registry IDs, never values
  • ongoing marks something kept up, such as a local webhook listener, and followUp says what the role does once the operator has acted

docs.title: Lists and states
docs.text:
• commits, pullRequests, versions and unblocks on actions, and waitingOn on blockers, are lists: a push covering several commits, a nested module's second tag on one commit, a blocker that waits on another role and then on the operator
  • An uncommitted state for finished work waiting on review; work in progress carries its state, so committed but unpushed work is listed once
  • Items carry versions; actions carry paths

docs.title: Session binding
docs.text:
plexushive -C my-hive start billing   # bind the role to this tmux session and print its context
plexushive -C my-hive context         # the same context, for a hook after start or compaction
plexushive whoami                     # the role and where it was found

Every command finds the role from --role, then HIVE_ROLE, then the tmux session's environment, so an agent started before the binding still finds it. report submit fills session.tmux inside tmux.

docs.title: Briefing
docs.text:
• A step several roles ask for is listed once with all their names: a push to the same repository and branch, or an action with the same kind, repository, branch and command
  • A role whose only open work waits on its own decision requests shows as decision, neither idle nor blocked
  • Actions show their versions, credentials, the actions they wait on, numbered steps and the role's follow-up

docs.title: Unreadable reports
docs.text: A report the reader cannot decode, such as one written by a newer version with fields it does not know, no longer stops the briefing. brief lists it under "Unreadable reports"; who, decide, context and report submit warn and carry on. From this release on, roles can move to a newer format one at a time.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• The schema carries the patterns validation applies: repositories, commits, pull requests, refs, credentials and role names
  • A pull request may be given as #<n> when one repository is named; it is stored as the full URL
  • asked accepts a date alone, though report submit sets it anyway

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
• hive.ResolveRole, hive.BindTmuxRole, hive.TmuxSession, hive.TmuxRole, hive.InTmux and the replaceable hive.Tmux
  • hive.NewContext, hive.Context and hive.Peer
  • hive.ReadReports, hive.UnreadableReport and (*hive.Briefing).SetUnreadable; hive.LoadReports stays strict
  • (*hive.Report).Normalize; hive.WriteReport normalizes before it validates
  • hive.Decision.Option, set by Decide
  • hive.RoleAction.Roles and Condition, and hive.Briefing.Waiting

docs.text: • report submit rejected a pull request given as #<n> even when the item or action named exactly one repository, because it validated the report before expanding the short form. It now expands first, and validation accepts #<n> wherever one repository is named.

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.5.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-22

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A hive record says what one long-lived agent is for and where it works. That is a work identity: a line of work, with a purpose and an address, that sessions take on. Until now plexushive called it a role, but role already has a settled meaning in access control, a permission level such as admin or viewer that a principal holds, and agents and people hold both kinds of record side by side. This release renames roles to work identities and leaves role to mean an access level.

Breaking changes for Go callers and JSON readers: the types, functions, directories, environment variable, flags and JSON fields are renamed (see below). Records, reports, sessions and scripts written for v0.4 keep working: reading accepts every old name, and writing uses only the new ones, so a hive can move over one session at a time.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
Before Now roles/<name>.json identities/<name>.json; a hive with both directories is refused HIVE_ROLE HIVE_IDENTITY, read first in the environment and in tmux --role --identity; --role still works and is deprecated plexushive roles <repo> plexushive identities <repo>; roles is an alias plexushive start <role> plexushive start <identity> "role" in a report "identity" "roles" in a decision "identities" role, roles in briefing and context JSON identity, identities contributor affinity collaborator, so it is not confused with a contributor access role plexushive schema role, role.schema.json plexushive schema identity, identity.schema.json

plexushive whoami says when it found the identity under HIVE_ROLE; run plexushive start <identity> again to bind the new variable.

docs.title: Moving a hive
docs.text:
1. Install v0.5.0 for every session on the machine first; earlier versions cannot read the new names.
  2. git mv roles identities in the hive directory, and replace "contributor" with "collaborator" in the records when convenient.
  3. Rebind each session with plexushive start <identity>. Reports and decisions move to the new field names the next time they are written.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text: • plexushive report show [identity] prints a work identity's stored report as JSON, to edit and submit again

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.6.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-22

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A decision request lasts only as long as a report carries it, and the open questions in a design record, such as an ADR's "Open questions" section, are in no report at all. This release adds open items: one list in the hive of every question waiting on the operator, wherever it was raised, kept until it is decided or withdrawn.

docs.title: Open items
docs.text:
open-items.json in the hive directory lists each question with its key (<identity>/<request id>), its source (a report, an ADR or another document), a status and the decision request:

Status Meaning draft A question with no options yet, such as one copied from an ADR open A complete decision request waiting on the operator deferred Waits on something its note names decided Answered by the decision it names withdrawn Dropped by its work identity without a decision

hive.Load reads the file and Hive.Validate checks it against the work identities and the decision log. A hive without the file has no open items.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
plexushive -C my-hive open                  # open, draft and deferred items, by status and work identity
plexushive -C my-hive open website --all    # one work identity's items, closed ones too
plexushive -C my-hive open sync             # update the list from the reports and the decision log
plexushive schema open-items

open sync adds requests not yet listed, opens a draft once its work identity asks a request with the same ID (this is how an ADR question gets its options), marks items answered by a decision as decided, and withdraws a report's question its work identity dropped without a decision. A work identity without a readable report is left as it is. decide marks the item it answers as decided.
